title: Divisorial indeterminacy of rational maps into group varieties
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ be a nonempty integral separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] smooth over $k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and let $G$ be a smooth connected separated finite-type $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $U\subseteq X$ be a dense open subscheme and $f:U\to G$ a $k$-morphism. Define the open subset
$$D=\bigcup\{V\subseteq X\text{ open}:U\subseteq V\text{ and there is a }k\text{-morphism }F_V:V\to G\text{ with }F_V|_U=f\}.$$
Then either $D=X$, or there exist $r\geq1$ and nonempty irreducible closed subsets $Z_1,\ldots,Z_r$ of $X$, with generic points $z_i$, such that
$$X\setminus D=\bigcup_{i=1}^r Z_i,\qquad \dim\mathcal O_{X,z_i}=1\quad(1\leq i\leq r).$$
Here generic means that the closure of $\{z_i\}$ equals $Z_i$, and dimension is Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Thus a nonempty indeterminacy locus is a finite union of prime divisors; properness of $G$ is not assumed.

source.place: 8.17, printed p.152; proof in literature/milne-abelian-varieties_AV.pdf, Chapter I, Lemma 3.3, printed pp.17–18. The union is the maximal domain of the rational map represented by (U,f).

proof.text: Put $Y=X\times_kX$. It is smooth: an affine first-order lifting problem for $Y$ is a pair of lifting problems for $X$, solved separately and paired by the fibre-product property. The locally finite presentation clause follows on affine charts by tensoring presentations: use both finite lists of generators and both finite lists of relations. The same chart description gives a finite affine cover of $Y$ from a finite affine cover of $X$. Thus $X$ and $Y$ are quasi-compact. Apply [lem-trf-smooth-geometrically-normal] over $k$ to $X$ and $Y$: both are regular, normal and reduced. Regularity includes local Noetherianity [def-weil-regular-scheme], so both are Noetherian. Their stalks are UFDs by [lem-trf-regular-local-regular-ring-ufd]; its extra regular-ring hypothesis holds because every prime localization of a stalk is the stalk at a generization, hence regular.

source.place: Tag 056T (lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal); regular-local UFD input is Tag 0AG0 (more-algebra.tex, lemma-regular-local-UFD); the product lifting and presentation arguments are written out.

proof.text: The underlying space of the Noetherian scheme $Y$ is Noetherian: a descending chain of closed subsets has a minimal member by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal]. Hence by [lem-trf-normal-topologically-noetherian-components], $Y$ is a finite disjoint union of open-and-closed integral schemes. Since $X$ is irreducible, its image under $\Delta$ is irreducible and lies in one component $W$; thus $\Delta:X\to W$ is defined. The open scheme $W$ is Noetherian with UFD stalks. Set $H_0=W\cap(U\times_kU)$ and $\phi(x,y)=f(x)f(y)^{-1}$ on $H_0$. It is nonempty since it contains $\Delta(U)$, hence dense in the integral $W$. Apply [lem-sfb-group-difference-diagonal-domain] with $\Omega=W$, obtaining $b:B\to G$ with $\Delta^{-1}B=D$ and $b\Delta=e$ on $D$. Its definition of $D$ allows domains not containing $U$: these give the same union as the item, since any such map glues with $f$ on $U$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing].

source.place: Chapter I, Lemma 3.3, p.17, difference-map argument; for the product component use Stacks Tag 0357 (properties.tex, lemma-normal-locally-finite-nr-irreducibles).

proof.text: Choose an affine open $T=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq G$ containing the identity point $e$, with $A$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra, using the finite-type affine charts. Put $H=\phi^{-1}(T)\subseteq H_0$ and $h=\phi|_H:H\to T$. Since $\phi\Delta=e$ on $U$ by the group identities [def-sc-group-scheme], $H$ contains $\Delta(U)$, so it is a dense open of $W$. Define $E$ as the union of the extension domains of $h$ as a map into $T$, exactly as in [lem-sfb-factorial-affine-rational-poles]. That node applies: $W$ is nonempty integral, Noetherian with UFD stalks, $H$ is dense, and $A$ is finitely generated. Obtain an effective Cartier divisor $P$ on $W$ with $|P|=W\setminus E$.

source.place: Chapter I, Lemma 3.3, pp.17–18, affine coordinates near e and their polar divisors.

proof.text: We claim $\Delta^{-1}(E)=D$. If $x\in D$, then $\Delta(x)\in B$ and $b(\Delta(x))=e$ by [lem-sfb-group-difference-diagonal-domain]. Restrict $b$ to the open $b^{-1}(T)$ in $B$; it extends $h$ on its intersection with $H$, so $\Delta(x)\in E$. Conversely, a $T$-valued representative on an open $N\subseteq W$ composed with $T\hookrightarrow G$ agrees with $\phi$ on $N\cap H$. The open $H$ is dense in $W$ and hence in $N\cap H_0$. This intersection is reduced, and $G$ is separated over $k$, so [lem-sfb-relative-separated-dominant-ext] extends that equality to $N\cap H_0$. Thus $N$ is a domain in the definition of $B$. Consequently $E\subseteq B$, giving $\Delta^{-1}E\subseteq\Delta^{-1}B=D$.

source.place: Chapter I, Lemma 3.3, pp.17–18, criterion for regularity at a diagonal point, with the affine-chart comparison made explicit.

proof.text: Let $Q=X\times_W P$ be the closed subscheme of $X$ defined by pulling back the local equations of $P$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. It is an effective Cartier divisor. Indeed, on a nonempty open $L\subseteq W$ where $P$ is cut out by a non-zero-divisor $t$, its inverse image in $X$ is either empty or an open containing the generic point of $X$. The generic point belongs to $U\subseteq D=\Delta^{-1}E$, so the image of $t$ at this generic point is a unit, in particular nonzero. On the integral open $\Delta^{-1}L$, the pulled-back section therefore has nonzero germ in every local domain: a zero germ would give zero at the generic point. It is a non-zero-divisor in each stalk, which is exactly the effective Cartier condition [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. Moreover $|Q|=\Delta^{-1}|P|=X\setminus D$. This also covers unit equations and the empty divisor.

source.place: Tag 02OO (lemma-pullback-effective-Cartier-defined), case (3); the integral-source local-equation proof is written out, with no flatness claim about the diagonal.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-factorial-cartier-prime-decomposition] to $Q$ on $X$, whose Noetherianity and UFD stalks were established in step 1. Its finite integral effective Cartier components have underlying nonempty irreducible closed subsets $Z_1,\ldots,Z_r$ and generic points $z_i$ with $\dim\mathcal O_{X,z_i}=1$. Their union is $|Q|=X\setminus D$: on stalks the product of the component ideals is a unit exactly when every factor is a unit. If $Q$ is empty, $D=X$. Otherwise the union is nonempty and at least one component occurs, so $r\geq1$. These are precisely the alternatives and the dimension assertion in the item.

source.place: Tags 0BCP (lemma-effective-Cartier-divisor-is-a-sum) and 0BCN (lemma-effective-Cartier-codimension-1 (2)); Milne AV, Lemma 3.3, final conclusion on p.18.

proof_origin.place: Chapter I, Lemma 3.3, printed pp.17–18; follows the difference-map/polar-divisor route, making the arbitrary-field product component and diagonal Cartier pullback explicit.
